title: Car dealership ripoff: Hidden-camera investigation
summary: An investigative report finds dealership service departments upselling unnecessary maintenance on commission while sometimes omitting a safety recall.

assertions.quote: They'll tell you that you need more maintenance than your car actually needs.

verdicts.note: Multiple investigations and consumer complaints document dealers routinely upselling service beyond factory schedules.

assertions.quote: People do not know they work on commission, but they do.

verdicts.note: Commission-based pay for service advisors is common industry-wide and creates a documented conflict of interest.

assertions.quote: they have made more on service than they have on selling new and used cars combined

verdicts.note: Service and parts are consistently the highest-margin department industry-wide, though outperforming combined vehicle sales varies by dealership.

assertions.quote: why wouldn't they have mentioned that to me?

verdicts.note: Documented lapses occur, though dealers generally have strong incentive and often a legal duty to disclose open recalls.

assertions.quote: This goes against what Chrysler says to do with its own product.

verdicts.note: Warranty validity is governed by the manufacturer's published maintenance schedule, not a dealer's upsold extras.
